done.why: The game turned into a sword duel where I kept typing 'attack figure' and got near-identical miss/parry lines. Nothing new was happening, so I quit.

about: A fantasy-dungeon sequel. You wake at the bottom of a stair, light a lantern, find a sword, and fight a hooded figure who seems to be testing you. A dream-wizard told you to prove yourself worthy.

moments.note: The sword I couldn't take at the junction appeared in my hand when I entered the Land of Shadow.
The figure disarmed me, then handed the sword back hilt first like a teacher. That made the duel feel meaningful.
The duel became repetitive: same 'too slow' and 'misses by a mile' lines, with no sense of progress.

wished: Some sign of how to win the duel, or a way around it
Something to do other than repeat attack

lines.line: It could end this. Instead it stoops, picks up your sword, and gives it back to you hilt first, the way a teacher does.
lines.why: It reframed the fight as a lesson and was the best moment.

fun.why: The opening was fine, but the duel was a repetitive slog.

engagement.why: I lost interest once the duel looped.

difficulty.why: I couldn't tell whether I was progressing in the fight.

interestingness.why: The teacher-like opponent and the sword that appeared from nowhere are intriguing.

prose.why: The prose is evocative and varied in the combat lines.
